title: Bound watchdog GitHub calls; retry only safe reads and reconcile uncertain writes
root_cause: The existing five-minute Required Gate Watchdog used raw fetch without an explicit per-request deadline or bounded transient GET retries, exposing the repair control plane to slow provider/network reads. This is a source-level risk, not proof of a past ChatGPT streaming fault.
impact: A provider stall or transient 429/502/503 can consume the watchdog execution budget and delay same-owner failure handoff; replaying ambiguous POST may duplicate comments/dispatches.
failed_approaches: Retrying ambiguous POST comments or workflow dispatches
Creating a second scheduler or writer
fix: Use AbortSignal.timeout(12000) on every watchdog GitHub call and at most two short retries only for GET transport exceptions/429/500/502/503/504. Never auto retry POST; resume on scheduled tick after marker/readback reconciliation.
prevention_rule: Every GitHub watchdog API call is deadline-bounded. Only idempotent GET reads may retry transient failure a fixed number of times. Any failed/ambiguous POST must not replay until durable side-effect readback. Preserve one canonical five-minute job and unchanged release gates.
outcome: CANDIDATE, awaiting exact-head Required/CodeQL and post-merge five-minute watchdog run
